short: Paired covert/overt vowel and consonant-class decoding on ECoG (M04) is ahead as a 2011 protocol; best-of-47–64-electrode selection and prompt-only covert labels make its gains upper bounds.
position: The paper [@pei2011decoding] changes two components. Its use-time action (M04) is ahead as a protocol: it discriminates vowel and consonant-pair classes in covert and overt repetition of the same 36 words within the same patients on ECoG, which no read prior does, confirming the authors' own "for the first time" claim (Sec. 1; Appendix). Its decoder (M06), one classifier per electrode with the best location reported, is standard for its time but departs from joint multi-electrode input. The overt result holds; the covert one rests on prompt-defined labels and on the best of 47–64 electrodes, and after a correction for that choice it survives in 2/6 patients for vowels and 1/6 for consonants (inference). Today a paired imagined/articulated design on high-density ECoG reaches 80.4% median imagined-syllable accuracy [@zhao2026neural], so this paper is a feasibility result, not a benchmark.
